defaults.time: none (ResourceLimits.max_feed_duration None, resource.rs:219). CodeMode integration applies 30 s per snippet when resource_limits is None.
defaults.memory: none (max_memory None, resource.rs:221). CodeMode integration applies 256 MiB when resource_limits is None.

source_notes.finding: Host functions are passed per feed as external_lookup (callables become host functions). Type-check stubs are separate (type_check_stubs, or ExternalModule stubs). No schema-driven generator at this layer; CodeMode builds stubs from each tool's JSON schema.
Monty itself exposes nothing to a model. CodeMode puts every eligible tool behind one run_code tool, so the model sees one tool and writes stubs-typed Python calls to the rest.

The sandbox runs in a subprocess reached over stdin and stdout pipes. A host call pauses the worker and returns a FunctionSnapshot. The host runs the function and calls resume. The snapshot can be dumped to about 2.2 KB and resumed in a new pool (snapshot_check.py).

The worker is a separate process started with env_clear, so the in-process claim in the article does not hold for v1.6. Unmounted filesystem access returns Permission denied, and os.environ and os.getenv raise not-supported. Host-side reality matches the probes (P3 to P5).
print() streams to print_callback. The return value is the last expression. Errors come back as MontyRuntimeError with frames. No truncation in the Monty API.

Library defaults are no time and no memory limit, with recursion and suspension caps. When configured, limits fire: max_feed_duration_secs=0.5 raised TimeoutError after 0.54 s, max_memory=50 MB raised MemoryError.
Session state persists across feeds in one checkout (REPL). A new checkout is fresh. Sessions dump with session.dump(), and mid-run state with FunctionSnapshot.dump().

The article's CodeExecutionToolset is not in pydantic-ai-slim 2.71.0. The shipped integration is pydantic_ai_harness CodeMode (0.71.0). It drives Monty through checkout plus feed_start and resume, and sets a 30 s and 256 MiB default.

surprises: Article hello-world (Monty(code, inputs=..., external_functions=...)) raises TypeError on 1.6.0: Monty.__new__() takes 0 positional arguments. The API is now a pool with checkout and feed_run (out/claims.txt).

Article says Monty starts in microseconds because it is embedded in the parent process. v1.6 runs every checkout in a monty subprocess (verified with pgrep). Measured warm feed 33 to 59 us, fresh checkout 0.05 to 0.14 ms median, against the article's 0.004 ms.

Article says the default is strict resource limits. The library default is none for time and memory (P6 never stops; P7 passes 4 GiB in 5 of 5 repeats). Limits only apply when configured or in the CodeMode integration.
Access claims hold: no filesystem, network, or env by default (P3 to P5), and P12 reaches no host object.
Snapshot dump is about 2.2 KB for a tiny state, which fits the article's single-digit-KB claim. Round trip across two pools works (out/snapshot.txt).
The article's CodeExecutionToolset does not exist in the pinned pydantic-ai-slim 2.71.0; use pydantic-ai-harness CodeMode instead.
Repo main (5f4a3dfc, v1.7.0-beta.1) is newer than the PyPI 1.6.0 the probes ran; pinned to the v1.6.0 tag. Source reading and the installed wheel match.
